lead: a man at a party spent about ninety seconds adjusting his estimate of you downward, and you watched the whole adjustment at a resolution he does not know exists. you still have his face from that evening.
sun: strangers meet a figure before they meet a person. across a room, in a queue, walking past you toward somebody else, the width does the introducing, and it introduces someone slightly better appointed than whoever eventually speaks. so first contact is always with a number you did not issue, arriving ahead of you, doing well, and handing the actual arrival a gap that nobody present has agreed to notice.
moon: what happens around the fourth minute is a settling in the other person's face as the number comes down to size, and you take it whole — the sentence it landed on, the exact half-second. none of that releases. so what you keep on strangers is not a file on strangers. it is a dated collection of the moments each of them worked out that the doorway had oversold you.
pull: the room invents a figure for you before you speak, then brings it down, and the bringing down is the part you keep. hundreds of them, dated, on people who never thought about you again.
tension: given plainly, the thing lands as fishing. people think slightly less of you at the fourth minute than at the first, and saying that out loud gets answered warmly, by somebody who is describing the first minute. the reassurance is sincere and it is evidence for what it denies. so it stops being said, and the widest, easiest person anybody knows keeps a private ledger of every downgrade ever taken on them.
cost: you can tell inside a minute which new person has settled where, and you are almost never wrong, so nothing in your life depends on a misread stranger. the settlings do not fade at your end and they do at theirs. a woman who revised you slightly downward at a wedding a decade ago has not thought about it since, and is still, tonight, revising you slightly downward.

lead: they have been calling you the obvious next one for six years. nothing has been decided anywhere, the seat is not vacant, and the word obvious is carrying the entire weight of an appointment nobody has had to make.
sun: a place choosing its next one is not choosing a worker. it is choosing something to be looked at, and you register at the size an institution that old wants at the head of its table. so you get sent — to the funeral, to the dinner with the money, to the room that needs the place to look larger than its accounts. each errand enters the record as evidence, and the evidence is width.
moon: nothing in you moves where the doubt sits, so it has never been in a room. you sit through the deferring, the seating plan, the joke about your inevitability, level throughout, and each year of not visibly wondering is read as somebody already doing the job. what you carry is not whether you want the chair. it is whether being the right size to picture there counts as a qualification.
pull: six years of being the next one, and no week in any of them where anybody found out whether you can do it. the seat is still occupied and you have already been given it.
tension: in the year it goes to somebody else, the room will need an account of why, and an assumption nobody made out loud cannot be disappointed out loud either — so the only material available will be you. a reason nobody can source is the shape a verdict takes when there was never a test on file. you will reach for the same account privately, and it will fit, and it will explain nothing.
cost: a place with a thin decade behind it still reads as a going concern with you at its table, which is worth more to it than most of what the building produces. none of that converts into a record. you can spend fifteen years being the reason a room takes an institution seriously and arrive at the end held up entirely by an impression formed at ten paces.

lead: nothing is being kept for later. no reserved version, no private amount, nothing that is not already out where a room can reach it, doubled — the size is the whole of the evidence and there is no second exhibit.
sun: a room does not experience being given anything by you. it experiences finding you already open — the time, the house, the name put forward, the afternoon — and helping itself, on the reasonable ground that nothing was shut. twenty years of this leaves no occasion anybody can point to where you decided in their favour. what people have of you they took, and none of it needed permission first.
moon: checking the size would take a withheld part to check it against, and no such part was fitted. what a room estimates at ten paces is also the only figure you own, so the suspicion that the portion was handed over rather than won cannot be settled at your end either. there is no unpublished remainder to weigh, nothing kept in the drawer as the true amount.
pull: everything is in the window. no stockroom, no reserve, no truer smaller one kept for the people who matter, so the estimate at the glass is the only figure either side has ever held.
tension: closeness elsewhere is proved by production — the thing said to one person and not the others, the version that only comes out after midnight. you have nothing to produce. a partner of eleven years works this out slowly and cannot say it without sounding ungrateful, because no complaint is available: nothing was refused, nothing was kept from them, and everything they hold of you a stranger could have inside an afternoon.
cost: anyone can have the whole of you in an hour. no queue, no earning it, no stretch at arm's length while you make up your mind about them, and it costs you nothing, which is also why it is not generosity — generosity needs a thing to have been held first. so nobody can be moved nearer, and the ones who stayed thirty years hold what the afternoon crowd holds.

lead: you still drive his mother to her appointments on thursdays. the thing that made her yours finished in you in a single season four years ago, and neither fact has ever been made to explain the other.
sun: nothing about an ending travels at this scale. what leaves you and lands on a room is width, and width is not a report on anybody's condition, so the season it went through you is entered nowhere. and an ending is when people ordinarily bring something — the dish, the evening, the call at a bad hour. nobody carries anything toward a doorway that reads as already well supplied.
moon: what finished, finished to the root: not less of the wanting, none of it, and no long dying middle where somebody could have caught it happening. the duties came through the same season without a mark on them, in their original condition, so you are still on the family calendar, still owed things, still owing them. what molted is the only part with no witness.
pull: the wanting went in one season and the thursdays did not. from any distance the arrangement looks unaltered, and any distance is the only place a person has ever stood to look at you.
tension: his sister worked it out before anyone, off nothing that was said, and the word she has settled on is cold. it is a fair reading of what she can see: every duty performed on time for four years with nothing inside it. the other account cannot be given from here, because a large, functioning, entirely unaltered person saying that something in them ended is heard as somebody laying the ground for leaving.
cost: nothing comes apart when something in you ends. the appointments hold, the family keeps its arrangement, the rota runs — all of it standing on a width that was never a feeling and does not go when the feeling goes. so the largest event of your decade is recorded nowhere, and the people it happened around have spent four years being looked after by someone they would describe as fine.
